name: Dale Pierce
life: “I still remember coffee going cold while the headlights turned back.” People around Maré Coffee know Dale by a small Monday habit. Dale likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I waited at the far end with coffee. I am proud that the first cup went cold and they still tried again.
appearance: Dale has thick, tightly coiled hair, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cropped bottle-green coat. It usually goes with a small enamel bird on the lapel. When somebody else has the floor, Dale rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Is a careful borrower and a reckless lender. Things leave this person's house with elaborate instructions and very little expectation of ever coming back.
agenda: To wait at the far end on another morning.
family: Kathleen Garza is Dale’s older cousin. Dale sets the time to leave. Kathleen picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The porch auction*, Kathleen says, “I left my weekly pay in the cushion years ago.”
connections: Sofia Valdez. A familiar song and a cup at the far end provide two markers for a practice drive.

reactions.situation: A friend insists the return journey must happen that night
reactions.response: Dale asks the learner when they want to try again, leaving the friend's timetable out of it.
